<STRUCT_0001>
Algebraic spaces were first introduced by Michael Artin,
see <REF_0001>, <REF_0002>,
<REF_0003>,
<REF_0004>,
<REF_0005>,
<REF_0006>,
<REF_0007>,
and <REF_0008>.
Some of the foundational material was developed jointly with
Knutson, who produced the book <REF_0009>.
Artin defined (see <REF_0010>)
an algebraic space as a sheaf for the <ACCENT_0001>tale topology
which is locally in the <ACCENT_0002>tale topology representable.
In most of Artin's work the categories of schemes
considered are schemes locally of finite type over a fixed
excellent Noetherian base.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
Our definition is slightly different from Artin's original definition.
Namely, our algebraic spaces are sheaves for the fppf topology
whose diagonal is representable and which have an <ACCENT_0003>tale ``cover''
by a scheme. Working with the fppf topology instead of the <ACCENT_0004>tale
topology is just a technical point and scarcely makes
any difference; we will show in
Bootstrap, Section <REF_0011>
that we would have gotten the same category of algebraic spaces
if we had worked with the <ACCENT_0005>tale topology. In that same chapter
we will prove that the condition on the diagonal
can in some sense be removed, see
Bootstrap, Section <REF_0012>.

<STRUCT_0004><STRUCT_0005>
After defining algebraic spaces we make some foundational observations.
The main result in this chapter is that with our definitions
an algebraic space is the same thing as an <ACCENT_0006>tale equivalence relation,
see the discussion in Section <REF_0013> and
Theorem <REF_0014>. The analogue of this theorem in
Artin's setting is <REF_0015>, or
<REF_0016>. In other words, the sheaf
defined by an <ACCENT_0007>tale equivalence relation has a representable diagonal.
It follows that our definition agrees with Artin's original definition
in a broad sense. It also means that one can give examples of algebraic
spaces by simply writing down an <ACCENT_0008>tale equivalence relation.

<STRUCT_0006><STRUCT_0007>
In Section <REF_0017> we introduce various separation
axioms on algebraic spaces that we have found in the literature.
Finally in Section <REF_0018>
we give some weird and not so weird examples of algebraic spaces.
